hza-ni10-242-p1.summary: Ferdinand III approves Hatzfeldt's plan for after the siege of Dorsten, has told Archduke Leopold Wilhelm to send him orders, and promises provisions, ammunition, foot, the Mandelsloh regiment and sixty Austrian ox-wagons for his march to Franconia.

hza-ni10-242-p2.summary: Preparations for the operation against Erfurt are under way (provisions from Leipzig); once Dorsten has fallen Hatzfeldt is to bring two half-cannon from "Statt Berg" and find horses to draw them.

hza-ni10-242-p3.summary: A postscript in a lighter hand recalls the order of the 7th about the guns from "Statt Berg"; four cipher letters are unresolved.

hza-ni10-242-p4.summary: Ciphered copy of the bond of Aachen: the city pays 20,000 reichsthalers within two months, raises 500 horse and pays the imperial contribution, in return for exemption from billeting.

hza-ni10-242-p5.summary: The Emperor lists the guns, powder, grain and wagons gathered at Würzburg and Leipzig for the Erfurt operation, urges Hatzfeldt not to delay after Dorsten, asks the Cardinal-Infante through Traun for 120,000 guilders owed to the Westphalian corps, and encloses the Aachen bond.
